questions.question: The simple interest on an amount for 6 years at 4% p.a. is ₹7,500 less than the simple interest on the same amount for 11 years. Find the amount.
questions.solution:
**Given:-**

 

SI for 11 years - SI for 6 years = ₹7,500 

**Formula used:- **

Simple Interest (SI) = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

**Calculation:-**

⇒ (P × 4 × 11) / 100 - (P × 4 × 6) / 100 = ₹7,500

⇒ (44P - 24P) / 100 = ₹7,500

⇒ 20P / 100 = ₹7,500

⇒ P = ₹37,500

**∴ The principal amount is ₹__37,500__.**31:T515,<str

A laptop is sold for Rs. 54,000 after a discount of 20%.

Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 - Discount%)

**Calculation:-**

The marked price of the laptop

⇒ MP = 54000/(80/100) 

⇒ MP = 67500

P, Q and R can complete a piece of work in 9, 12 and 18 days, respectively. Working together, how much work can they complete in one day?
questions.solution:
**Detailed solution:-**

P, Q, and R can complete a work in 9, 12, and 18 days, respectively. 

Rate of P = 1/9 (work/day)

Rate of Q = 1/12 (work/day)

Rate of R = 1/18 (work/day)

Combined rate = Rate of P + Rate of Q + Rate of R

= 1/9 + 1/12 + 1/18 = (4 + 3 + 2)/36 = 9/36 = 1/4 (work/day)

**∴ when P, Q, and R work together, they can complete 1/4 of the work in one day.**

questions.question: Ram and Ramesh can do a work in 12 days, Ramesh and Somesh in 15 days and Somesh and Ram in 10 days. If Ram, Ramesh and Somesh work together, in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ram and Ramesh can do work together =12 days

Ramesh and Somesh can do work together = 15 days

Somesh and Ram can do work together = 10 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the Ram, Ramesh, and Somesh can complete the work together in X days

One day work of Ramesh and Ram = {1over12}

One day work of Ramesh and Somesh = {1over15}

One day work of Somesh and Ram = {1over10}

One day work of all three = {1over12}+{1over15}+{1over10} = {5+4+6over60}={15over60}={1over4}

Working twice they can complete the work in = 4 days

They can complete the work = 8 days

**∴ The required result will be 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Calculation:**

Ram and Ramesh = 12 days

Ramesh and Somesh = 15 days

Somesh and Ram = 10 days 

LCM of (12,15, & 10) = 60 units

Efficiency of Ram and Ramesh = 60/12 = 5 units

Efficiency of Ramesh and Somesh = 60/15 = 4 units

Efficiency of Somesh and Ram = 60/10 = 6 units

Efficiency of 2(Ram, Ramesh & Somesh) = 15 units(5 + 4 + 6)

Total Efficiency of Ram, Ramesh & Somesh = (5 + 4 + 6)/2 = 7.5 units

Time taken by Ram, Ramesh, and Somesh together to complete the work:

Time = Total work / Total Efficiency

⇒ 60/7.5 = 8 days 

**∴ Ram, Ramesh, and Somesh together will complete the work in 8 days.**

A dishonest dealer sells articles at 15% loss on cost price but uses the weight of 20 g instead of 25 g. What is his profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A dishonest dealer sells articles at 15% loss on cost price.

**Concept:**

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

**Formula used:**

P\%={SP-CPover CP}× 100 Where, P = Profit, SP = Selling price, and CP = Cost price

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the 25 g article be X.

The selling price of the article = {(1 - {15over 100})} × X={({100-15over100})} × X={85over100} × X=0.85X

The cost price of the 20g article = {Xover 25} × 20={4Xover5}

The profit percentage = {0.85X-0.8Xover0.8X}× 100={0.05Xover 0.8X}× 100={0.0625 × 100}=6.25\%

**∴ The required result will be 6.25% Profit.**

SP > CP so it is profit

Profit% = (1/16) × 100 = 6.25% profit.

∴ The required result will be 6.25% Profit.

questions.question: If (a + b + c) = 14, and (a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc) = 98, find the value of (a² + b² + c²).
questions.solution:
Given:

a + b + c = 14

a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc = 98

Concept used:

a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc = (a + b + c)[(a + b + c)² - 3(ab + bc + ca)]

Calculation:

a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = (a + b + c)[(a + b + c)2 - 3(ab + bc + ca)]

⇒ 98 = 14 × [(14)² - 3(ab + bc + ca)]

⇒ 7 = 196 - 3(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 189 = 3(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ ab + bc + ca = 63

(a + b + c)2 = (a2 + b2 + c2) + 2(ab + bc + ca)]

(a2 + b 2 + c2) = 14² - 2 × 63

= 196 - 126

= 70

∴ The value of given identities is 70.

questions.question: A 6-digit number has digits as consecutive natural numbers. The number is always divisible by _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept used**

Any 6-digit number formed by a consecutive natural number is always divisible by 3 because the sum of digits of any such number is divisible by 3.

**Calculation**

For ex. take 123456, 234567, 345678, and 456789, as a number, the sum of its digit is always divisible by 3.

**The answer is 3.**

questions.question: The distance between the centres of two circles having radii 22 cm and 18 cm, is 32 cm. The length (in cm) of the direct common tangent of the two circles is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of bigger circle r₁ = 22 cm

Radius of smaller circle r₂ = 18 cm

Distance between two circles = 32 cm

**Formula used:**

Length of direct tangent, l = sqrt {d² - (r₁ - r₂)²} 

Where, d = Distance between two circles,

r₁ = Radius of bigger circle, r₂ = Radius of smaller circle

**Calculation:**

According to the question

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff4f4a9180a640f415d2f5fdffa3ed7941cc0b79f609403bc7861b6a7d0bfd38.png] 

The length of the direct tangent (I)

⇒ sqrt{32²-(22-18)²}

⇒ sqrt{32²-4²} 

⇒ sqrt{1024-16}

⇒ sqrt{1008} = 2sqrt{252} cm

**∴ The required result will be 2sqrt{252} cm.**

questions.question: The length of a hall is 21 m and the width is 14 m. The sum of the areas of the floor and the flat roof is equal to the sum of the areas of the four walls. Find the height of the hall.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The length of the hall = 21 m

The width of the hall = 14 m

**Formula used:**

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth

Area of four wall of rectangular hall = 2 × (Length + Breadth) × Height

Volume of cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

**Calculation:**

Let the height of the hall be H

Area of floor = 21 × 14 = 294 m²

Sum of floor and ceiling = 294 + 294 = 588 m²

The area of the four walls of the hall = 2 × (21 + 14) × H = 70H

According to the question

⇒ 70H = 588

⇒ H = {588over70}=8.4 m

**∴ The required result will be 8.4 m.**

questions.question: If sec A + tan A = 5,then sin A is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

sec A + tan A = 5

**Concept used:**

If sec A + tan A = x then,

⇒ sec A - tan A = 1/x

**Formula used:**

Sin θ = P/H ; sec θ = H/B ; tan θ = P/B

Pythagorean theorem:

 H2 = P2 + B2

Where, H = hypotenuse ; P = perpendicular ; B = base

**Calculation:**

⇒ sec A + tan A = 5 ------- (1)

then,

⇒ sec A - tan A = 1/5 -------- (2)

Adding the eq.(1) and (2)

⇒ Sec A + tan A + sec A - tan A = 5 + (1/5)

⇒ 2 × sec A = 26/5

⇒ sec A = 13/5 = H/B

By Pythagorean theorem:

⇒ H² = P² + B²

⇒ (13)² = P² + 5²

⇒ P² = 169 - 25 = 144

⇒ P = √144 = 12 

Sin A = P/H = 12/13

**∴ The correct answer is 12/13.**
